nodes.summary: In a complete uniformly convex space, a minimizing sequence for the distance from a point `x` to a closed convex set `K` converges to a point of `K` attaining that distance. The argument is the usual one: if the sequence were not Cauchy, two far-apart almost-minimizing terms would have normalized displacements far apart on the unit sphere, and uniform convexity would force their midpoint to beat the infimum,…
nodes.title: Convergence of minimizing sequences in uniformly convex spaces

nodes.summary: In a finite-dimensional strictly convex space, a minimizing sequence for the distance to a closed convex set supplies a unique nearest point. The uniqueness clause only assumes that a second point belongs to the set and attains the distance; it does not assume that the minimizing sequence converges to that point.
nodes.title: Unique nearest point from a minimizing sequence in finite dimensions

nodes.summary: In a finite-dimensional strictly convex space, a minimizing sequence for the distance to a closed convex set converges to the unique point of the set attaining that distance. This preserves the original combined API as a corollary of nearest-point uniqueness and minimizing-sequence convergence.
nodes.title: Minimizing sequences converge to the unique nearest point

nodes.summary: In finite dimensions, strict convexity and uniform convexity are equivalent.
nodes.title: Strict and uniform convexity agree in finite dimensions

nodes.summary: In a finite-dimensional real normed space, strict convexity implies uniform convexity. The proof maximizes `‖x + y‖` over the compact set of pairs of unit vectors at distance at least `ε`; strict convexity says the maximum is `< 2`, and the gap is the required `δ`.
nodes.title: Strict convexity implies uniform convexity in finite dimensions
